analysis:
The PR is a documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. The visible patch adds two rows at head lines 553-555 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION. Both are memory/latency tuning controls: an idle buffer-cache sweep gated on whole-Mac idleness, and retention of free KV segments in paged pools. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the second row (after "New segments") was not visible and I could not read it. The rows are documented as exact-`0`-disables, default-on and forwarded to launchd. They claim retained KV segments are "uncommitted and uncharged", dropped on refused admission, on memory pressure and before load gates, and after 30 s idle.

Security relevance: retained free KV segments could in principle hold residual decrypted prompt/KV data in memory (T-028, A-001, TB-007). The documentation says they are free and reinstalled at admission. No source code is in this batch, so whether segments are zeroed or overwritten before reuse cannot be verified. The doc does not claim that. Retention adds no network or auth surface. Neither control touches the SSD prefix cache (T-041), its HMAC lookup tags, TTL or encryption, or attestation and authorization (TB-011). Forwarding the two variables to launchd widens the operator-controlled environment passthrough only for opt-out values, which are operator-owned within TB-003. No concrete regression is established by this doc change.

Remaining questions for integration: the code in GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, KVPoolReclaimer.swift and EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift is not in this batch. Whether retained KV segments are cleared or overwritten on reuse, and whether the memory accounting stays correct (an availability point), should be confirmed there. The T-028 residual-GPU-memory assumption may deserve a note if retention extends the lifetime of stale KV buffers beyond the previous behavior. This is unverified from the docs alone.
